column1: # Game profile of Brain Memory Training Academy (Switch, base game v0). Plays on the Mac and on the iPhone

# Unity 2022.3.5f1 (IL2CPP), SDK 16.2.4: the shaders are Shader objects in the player's serialized files (Data/*.assets, no bundles), which carry no type trees; unityfs.py has Unity 2022.3's Shader layout (KNOWN_TREES)
# Controller only (stick or D-pad, A, B, +): the game never reads the touch screen, so it stays docked (1920x1080) with the default 2D pad layout

# Game name: only a label for profile listings and the Mac window title; the iOS app name is the game name in the base NSP, and the bundle ID comes from the base game title ID (build_ipa.sh / NSP script)
# load order as on Horizon: main, subsdk*, sdk (subsdk0 = NintendoSDK_movie)

# The NPDM declares 16 MB of system resource, so IsVirtualAddressMemoryEnabled is true: nninitStartup (main+0x73ad60) hands application pool − used memory to StandardAllocator as virtual address memory

# and never calls SetMemoryHeapSize. The node area cut for this sdk build (dm/tools/sdk_patches.py) shrinks the AddressRegionManager's node area to 62 MB, as for Ace Attorney Investigations Collection.
# Measured with probes on VammManager::AllocateAddressRegion's success path (sdk+0x1348b8: x21 size, x22 address) and FreeAddressRegion (sdk+0x135100): StandardAllocator takes 960 MB at +64 MB,

# Unity's own regions (main+0x11bb4cc) hold about 0.54 GB more, and over four minutes of level loads the live regions end at +2.0 to +2.1 GB; in 20 minutes the mapped high-water mark stopped at +2.51 GB
# (about 4 minutes in), at most 0.5 GB mapped, about 0.75 GB resident on the Mac. So Ace Attorney Investigations Collection's layout: a 1 GB pool and the 5 GB block
# (256 MB in front + 4.375 GB alias region + 256 MB stack region + 128 MB heap region)
# ---- Shader split (shader_split.py; Unity Shader objects, read by unityfs.py) ----
# engine built-ins (Resources/: unity default resources, unity_builtin_extra) go to engine, the player's serialized files to data
